pages.hook: A big American supermarket can feel like a small town, with numbered aisles and signs everywhere. Learn how to find milk, bread and rice, and how to ask for help.

mythfact.s: In the USA, people push a “cart” in the supermarket.
mythfact.why: In British English the same thing is called a “trolley”.

mythfact.s: Aisles in a supermarket often have numbers and signs.
mythfact.why: The signs list the products, so you can find them quickly.

mythfact.s: Honolulu is in the state of Hawaii.
mythfact.why: Honolulu is the capital city of Hawaii, on the island of Oahu.

mythfact.s: Staff in a store are never happy to help.
mythfact.why: Asking “Excuse me, where is…?” is normal and polite.

mythfact.s: You must always pay a tip at the supermarket.
mythfact.why: Tips are for services like restaurants. At a supermarket, you do not tip.

lines: Fresh bread is now ready in aisle 4.
Thank you for shopping with us.

decode.why: “Fresh bread is now ready in aisle 4.”

compare.br: In Brazil, people often say “Moço, onde fica o leite?” and the staff may walk with you to the shelf.
compare.us: In the USA, a worker may point and say “Aisle three, on the left”, and the signs help you a lot.
compare.tip: Use “Excuse me” first, then ask: Where is…? Do you have…?
compare.ask: Where is the milk in your supermarket? Say it in English.

quiz.q: You want to ask a worker for the milk. You say…
opts: Excuse me, where is the milk?
quiz.why: Excuse me, where is…? is polite.

quiz.q: “It’s next to the milk.” Next to means…

quiz.why: Say the aisle, then the side.

Reading quest — Lost in a big store · part 1
text: Today I went shopping in **Honolulu**. The supermarket was huge, and I felt lost. I needed milk, bread and rice, but I did not know where they were.

I saw a young worker. “**Excuse me, where is the milk?**” I asked. “**It’s in aisle three**,” she said. Then I asked, “**And where is the bread?**” “**It’s next to the milk**,” she said. That was easy!

I pushed my cart and found the milk. It was cold and fresh. Then I asked, “**Do you have rice?**” She smiled. “**Yes, in aisle five, on the left.**” “**Thank you!**” I said. “**You’re welcome**,” she answered. “**Happy shopping!**”

fast.why: The writer asks for milk, bread and rice.

scan.q: Which side is the rice on?

tf.s: The supermarket is very small.
tf.why: The supermarket was huge.

tf.s: The rice is in aisle five.
tf.why: “Yes, in aisle five, on the left.”

tf.s: The writer does not need help.
tf.why: The writer asks the worker for help.

tf.s: The writer buys milk, bread and rice.
tf.why: The last paragraph lists them.

text: I thought about the old rhyme Baa, Baa, Black Sheep. The sheep has “three bags full” of wool. My basket was not full of wool, but it was full of food. A simple shopping day can feel like a little song.
